title: Higher-order functions: taking and returning behaviour

videos.script: A method that takes a lambda, or returns one, is called a higher-order function. You have used several already. This lesson writes them. {{take}} First, three methods that differ in one line: longer than, cheaper than, by this author. One method that takes the line as an argument replaces all three, and every one somebody has not thought of yet. {{return}} Then the other direction. A method that returns a lambda is a factory of rules. Ask it for books of at least four hundred and fifty pages and it hands you a test. {{wrap}} A function can also take a function and return a better one: one that logs every call, or remembers its answers. {{map}} And last, a pricing rule chosen by name from a map, where a design pattern used to need an interface and three classes.
